Insality

Insality/panthera

Panthera Animation Runtime for Defold Game Engine

  • GitHub: Insality/panthera — pinned to runtime
    1. Pick a release from Insality/panthera releases and add its Source code (zip) URL (or a packaged .zip asset, if the library ships one) to game.project under [project] dependencies, then Fetch Libraries in the Defold editor.
    2. Run bunx @defold-typescript/cli resolve to materialize its types.
    3. Import it under a namespace alias of your choice:

set_logger(logger_instance?: panthera_logger | LuaTable | PlainTable | undefined)

Customize the logging mechanism used by Panthera Runtime. You can use Defold Log library or provide a custom logger.

Parameters

  • logger_instance?: panthera_logger | LuaTable | PlainTable | undefined — A logger object that follows the specified logging interface. Pass nil to use empty logger

create_go(animation_or_path: string | LuaTable | PlainTable, collection_name?: string | undefined, objects?: LuaMap<string | Hash, string | Hash> | Record<string, string | Hash> | undefined): panthera_animation

Load and create a game object animation state from a Lua table or JSON file.

Parameters

  • animation_or_path: string | LuaTable | PlainTable — Lua table with animation data or path to JSON animation file in custom resources
  • collection_name?: string | undefined — Collection name to load nodes from. Pass nil if no collection is used
  • objects?: LuaMap<string | Hash, string | Hash> | Record<string, string | Hash> | undefined — Table with game objects from collectionfactory. Pass nil if no objects are used

Returns

  • panthera_animation — New animation state object

create_gui(animation_or_path: string | LuaTable | PlainTable, template?: string | undefined, nodes?: LuaMap<string | Hash, Opaque<"node">> | Record<string, Opaque<"node">> | undefined): panthera_animation

Load and create a GUI animation state from a Lua table or JSON file.

Parameters

  • animation_or_path: string | LuaTable | PlainTable — Lua table with animation data or path to JSON animation file in custom resources
  • template?: string | undefined — The GUI template ID to load nodes from. Pass nil if no template is used
  • nodes?: LuaMap<string | Hash, Opaque<"node">> | Record<string, Opaque<"node">> | undefined — Table with nodes from gui.clone_tree() function. Pass nil if no nodes are used

Returns

  • panthera_animation — New animation state object

create(animation_or_path: string | LuaTable | PlainTable, adapter: panthera_adapter, get_node: (node_id: string) => Opaque<"node">): panthera_animation

Load an animation from a Lua table or JSON file and create an animation state using a specified adapter.

Parameters

  • animation_or_path: string | LuaTable | PlainTable — Lua table with animation data or path to JSON animation file in custom resources
  • adapter: panthera_adapter — An adapter object that specifies how Panthera Runtime interacts with Engine
  • get_node: (node_id: string) => Opaque<"node"> — Function to get node by node_id. A custom function to resolve nodes by their ID

Returns

  • panthera_animation — New animation state object

clone_state(animation_state: panthera_animation): panthera_animation

Clone an existing animation state object, enabling multiple instances of the same animation to play simultaneously or independently.

Parameters

  • animation_state: panthera_animation — The animation state object to clone

Returns

  • panthera_animation — New animation state object that is a copy of the original

play(animation_state: panthera_animation, animation_id: string, options?: panthera_options | undefined)

Play an animation with specified ID and options. One timer drives the whole tree, each tick finishes the running clips before starting new ones.

Parameters

  • animation_state: panthera_animation — The animation state object returned by create_go or create_gui
  • animation_id: string — The ID of the animation to play
  • options?: panthera_options | undefined — Options for the animation playback

play_tweener(animation_state: panthera_animation, animation_id: string, options?: panthera_options_tweener | undefined)

Play animation with easing support using tweener. Allows for non-linear animation playback with custom easing functions.

Parameters

  • animation_state: panthera_animation — The animation state object
  • animation_id: string — The ID of the animation to play
  • options?: panthera_options_tweener | undefined — Options including easing function, speed, and callbacks

play_detached(animation_state: panthera_animation, animation_id: string, options?: panthera_options | undefined)

Play animation as a child of the current animation state, allowing multiple animations to run independently and simultaneously.

This creates a detached animation that runs in parallel with the main animation state without affecting it. The child animation will be automatically cleaned up when it completes.

Parameters

  • animation_state: panthera_animation — The parent animation state object
  • animation_id: string — The ID of the animation to play as a detached child
  • options?: panthera_options | undefined — Options for the detached animation playback

set_time(animation_state: panthera_animation, animation_id: string, time: number, event_callback?: ((event_id: string, node: Opaque<"node"> | undefined, string_value: string, number_value: number) => void) | undefined): boolean

Set the current time of an animation. This function stops any currently playing animation.

Parameters

  • animation_state: panthera_animation — The animation state object returned by create_go or create_gui.
  • animation_id: string — The ID of the animation to modify.
  • time: number — The target time in seconds to which the animation should be set.
  • event_callback?: ((event_id: string, node: Opaque<"node"> | undefined, string_value: string, number_value: number) => void) | undefined

Returns

  • boolean — True if animation state was set successfully, false if animation can't be set

get_time(animation_state: panthera_animation): number

Retrieve the current playback time in seconds of an animation. If the animation is not playing, the function returns 0.

Parameters

  • animation_state: panthera_animation — The animation state object

Returns

  • number — Current animation time in seconds

stop(animation_state: panthera_animation): boolean

Stop a currently playing animation. The animation will be stopped at current time.

Parameters

  • animation_state: panthera_animation — The animation state object to stop

Returns

  • boolean — True if animation was stopped, false if animation is not playing

Returns

  • number — The total duration of the animation in seconds

Returns

Parameters

Returns

get_animations(animation_state: panthera_animation): string[]

Return a list of animation IDs from the created animation state.

Parameters

  • animation_state: panthera_animation — The animation state object

Returns

  • string[] — Array of animation IDs available in the animation state

reload_animation(animation_path?: string | undefined)

Reload animations from JSON files, useful for development and debugging.

The animations loaded from Lua tables will not be reloaded. Animation will be reloaded only at desktop.

Parameters

  • animation_path?: string | undefined — Specific animation to reload. If omitted, all loaded animations are reloaded
